title: Three decades of simulating global temperature patterns with coupled global climate models
abstract: Abstract Accurately simulating the climate system has been a challenge and aspiration since the advent of numerical modeling. Here, we use the spatial pattern of 2 m surface temperature to discuss the evolution of model performance from the beginning of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP) in the 1990s to the latest kilometer-scale models today. We find that the kilometer-scale IFS-FESOM model outperforms even the best CMIP6 models, while other kilometer-scale models still have considerable deficits. These results demonstrate the potential of kilometer-scale models to surpass established CMIP models, despite undergoing only limited tuning, while also highlighting the considerable efforts still needed to realize their full potential. We put this performance in the context of 10 observation-based references and 150 coupled global climate models developed over the past three decades to discuss that increasing resolution might be necessary, but is not sufficient for improving model skill.
problem: Accurately assessing long-term climate model improvement is challenging because simply increasing resolution is insufficient, and reliance on a single observational reference dataset increasingly biases performance evaluations as model skill improves, obscuring true progress.
method: This paper evaluates the evolution of climate model performance by comparing simulated 2m surface air temperature patterns from 176 models against an uncertainty range defined by 10 observation-based reference datasets.
task: The task is to evaluate the evolution of coupled global climate model performance over three decades by comparing their simulations of global temperature patterns against ten observation-based reference datasets, from early CMIP models to modern kilometer-scale models.
innovation: This paper evaluates three decades of global climate models against 10 observational references, demonstrating that while new kilometer-scale models can outperform previous generations, increased resolution alone is not sufficient for improving skill.
